clue.text: Inflate a price to tour England's capital

indicators.note: to tour a place is to travel all round it, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: taken as written
a price is a rate, as in the going rate

indicators.note: a capital is the head letter at the start of a word, so only the first is kept

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper puffs up a price for visitors touring England's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'England's capital' looks like London, but here it means the capital letter of England, which sits inside A RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To aerate is to fill with air, which is what you do when you blow up or pump up something.

clue.text: Mostly silk product from France

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: a silk is a senior barrister (a King's Counsel, who wears a silk gown), and a barrister is a brief in slang

explanation.surface: An item made mostly of silk, imported from France.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a silk is a senior barrister and a brief is informal for a barrister, so silk gives BRIEF, and 'mostly' trims it to BRIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft cheese originating in the Île-de-France region, so it is a French product.

clue.text: Soviet police man breaking sticks off

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece goes inside another
something off has gone bad or is out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange
a man is referred to as he

explanation.surface: A Soviet policeman snaps off some sticks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Police man' reads as one word, policeman, but it splits: 'Soviet police' is the definition and 'man' is a pronoun breaking into the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cheka was the early Soviet secret police force, and its agents were called Chekists.

clue.text: 501 stars producing records

parts.note: in Roman numerals D is 500 and I is 1
Aries is a constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: Five hundred and one celebrities release records, as if a label's roster had a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The number is read as Roman numerals, DI, and 'stars' is one particular constellation of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Diaries are daily written accounts of events, kept as personal records of one's life.

clue.text: Innovator in camp up and about

indicators.note: and simply adds one piece after another in sequence
in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a camp is a faction or side in a dispute
about in the sense of concerning, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: An inventor is at a camp and has just got up and is walking about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camp up and about' sounds like someone waking in a tent; 'camp' is a faction, SIDE, turned upward, with ON for 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the prolific American inventor of the phonograph and practical electric light bulb, a famous example of an innovator.

clue.text: Invalid felt sicker, having come out in most spots

definitions.text: having come out in most spots

indicators.note: something invalid is not sound or proper, so the letters are out of order and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A sick patient felt worse after breaking out in a rash of spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invalid' reads as a noun for a sick person, which fits the illness; it is really the adjective meaning not sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Freckles are small brown marks on the skin, so the freckliest person has broken out in the greatest number of them.

clue.text: Father has something inherited with value

parts.note: a gene is a unit of heredity passed from parent to child
to rate something is to value it

explanation.surface: A father owns a valuable heirloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father' looks like a noun, a parent, but it is the verb meaning to beget.
explanation.definitionFit: To father something is to bring it into being or produce it, the same sense as the verb generate.

clue.text: Warm area of hard ground

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
earth is the ground beneath our feet

explanation.surface: A sunny patch on otherwise hard, frozen ground.
explanation.walkthrough: H for hard is the mark used on pencils, as in HB.
explanation.definitionFit: The hearth is the floor of a fireplace, the spot in a home where it is warmest.

clue.text: Ruling party on the left, around south, is supported uncommonly

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece is placed on both sides of another

parts.note: a party in power is said to be in
a do is a party or celebration
red is the colour of the political left
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A left-wing ruling party is backed by an unusual coalition, with the south of the country on side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruling party' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces, and red is the traditional colour of the left. 'Uncommonly' tells you the answer is a rarer spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Indorsed is a rare variant spelling of endorsed, meaning backed or approved, so the definition flags its unusual form.

clue.text: After joint, do giggle

indicators.note: after tells us which piece comes second, so order is set by this word

parts.note: J is slang for a cannabis joint
to do someone is to imitate them, to ape them

explanation.surface: Someone who has smoked a joint goes on to giggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' as in doing an impression of someone gives APE; 'giggle' is a noun here, a bit of fun.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a giggle can be a bit of fun or a lark, as is a jape, a practical joke.

clue.text: Extremely knavish career by communist playing the communist reformer

indicators.note: extremely points at the extremes, the two outermost letters of a word

parts.note: the first and last letters
to career is to rush headlong
Che Guevara, the Marxist revolutionary
v, for versus, as in a fixture list where one team is playing another

explanation.surface: A villainous career spent playing a part alongside another communist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' is the verb meaning rush, not a job; 'playing' is v, as in Arsenal v Chelsea.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikita Khrushchev led the Soviet Union after Stalin and is known for his de-Stalinisation reforms.

clue.text: I need to think the French paper's dropped one pair of Europeans

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: something dropped is let fall and left out, so it is removed

parts.note: The Times, a British newspaper
one as a Roman numeral, the letter taken out
E is the abbreviation for European, twice

explanation.surface: Someone muses on why a French newspaper let two European correspondents go.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times is the London daily newspaper; with its I dropped it becomes TMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Let me see is a spoken filler used while pausing to consider something, much like saying you need a moment's thought.

clue.text: Element sculpted with art in lintel

indicators.note: sculpted material is reshaped into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A decorative element carved into a stone lintel above a door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the two words whose letters are mixed together.
explanation.definitionFit: A manteltree is the beam or stone across the top of a fireplace opening, a kind of lintel.

clue.text: Treated ailing ruminant in Asia

indicators.note: something treated has been worked on and changed, so these letters are altered in order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A vet has treated a sick cud-chewing animal somewhere in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treated ailing' reads as medical care for a sick animal, but 'treated' is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The nilgai, or blue bull, is a large antelope of India and Pakistan, and antelopes chew the cud.

clue.text: Puts forward large packaging deal

indicators.note: packaging wraps round its contents, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size
deal is softwood timber such as pine

explanation.surface: A company proposes a big packaging contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' looks like a business agreement but is the timber sense, as in a deal table.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state a view, so someone who opines is putting forward their opinion.

clue.text: Pro wrestling with medal for a prize

indicators.note: wrestlers twist and tangle, so these letters are contorted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A professional wrestler competes for a medal as a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pro wrestling' reads as the entertainment sport, but 'wrestling' is the signal to mix up PRO and MEDAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Palme d'Or is the top award given at the Cannes Film Festival each year.

clue.text: Province that's eight steps behind India?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the French-speaking Canadian province
second meaning: in the phonetic alphabet India is I, and counting eight letters on from I lands on Q

explanation.walkthrough: India here is not the country but the codeword for I in the NATO phonetic alphabet; the question mark flags the playful counting.
explanation.definitionFit: Quebec is both a large Canadian province and the NATO radio codeword for the letter Q.

clue.text: Diddly-squat, or zero, is round number in piquet

indicators.note: the outer words sit round the solution, enclosing it within their letters

parts.note: the letters run on across the words, ignoring the comma and space

explanation.surface: A card player scores diddly-squat, zero, in a round of piquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round number' looks like a whole number such as fifty; the phrase splits so that 'is round' signals the enclosure and the definition is 'number in piquet'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the card game piquet, a quatorze is a set of four aces, kings, queens, jacks or tens, scoring fourteen points.

clue.text: Fish hearts, but not hat, could be articles on boats

indicators.note: but not means excluding, so these letters are taken away

parts.note: the rudd is a freshwater fish
taken as written
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: Fish hearts, but no hat, might be things you'd find stored on board a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'hat' need not be together in 'hearts': each is removed separately, and the rudd is a small European freshwater fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A rudder is the hinged blade at a vessel's stern used for steering, a standard fitting on boats.

clue.text: Most scheming to get agreement accepted by special officer

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for special

indicators.note: what is accepted is taken in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer
yes is a word of agreement

explanation.surface: The most devious operator gets a deal approved by a special agent.
explanation.walkthrough: S for special is a crossword abbreviation; the agreement word goes inside LT, the officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sly means cunning and underhand, so the slyest person is the most scheming and crafty.

clue.text: Dogs are, we hear, wearing formal evening attire

indicators.note: whatever wears clothing is inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: tails are a tailcoat, worn for white-tie occasions

indicators.note: we hear points to what is heard, so a sound stands in for letters

parts.note: the word is pronounced like the letter R

explanation.surface: Dogs, it's said, are dressed up in formal evening wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dogs' reads as the animals, but it is the verb, to follow closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them persistently, the same as to trail them or shadow them.

clue.text: Doctor cut a vein? It's not working

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered in order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A medic asks whether cutting a vein would help, and is told the treatment isn't working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the physician, which suits the vein, but it is the verb meaning to tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: Unactive is an uncommon form of inactive, describing something idle or not operating.

clue.text: Child, under six, framing current image

indicators.note: in a down entry, being under means coming lower down, so order is fixed by this word

parts.note: six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: a frame surrounds a picture, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: a son is a child
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A young child with a picture of a flowing river framed around it.
explanation.walkthrough: I is the symbol for current in physics formulas; in a down clue the child sits below the six.
explanation.definitionFit: A vision is a mental picture or something seen in the mind's eye, so it is an image.

clue.text: Which person arrests attendant moving ecstasy in novel?

indicators.note: to arrest someone is to hold them in custody, so one piece holds another

parts.note: who asks which person

indicators.note: moving the drug's letter shifts just that one letter to a new position while the rest stay put

parts.note: a steward attends passengers on a ship or plane

explanation.surface: A detective novel: someone arrests a flight attendant carrying ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: E is crossword shorthand for the drug ecstasy; only that letter of the attendant moves, to the front, before being held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Westward Ho! is an 1855 adventure novel by Charles Kingsley, which gave its name to a Devon village.

clue.text: Axes by stone portico in Greece

parts.note: x and y are the two axes of a graph
st is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight

explanation.surface: Axes lie beside a stone colonnade in ancient Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axes' looks like chopping tools, but it is the plural of axis. A stone is a British unit of weight, 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A xyst was a long covered colonnade in ancient Greek gymnasiums where athletes exercised in winter.

clue.text: Unknown fish bones may appear in this

parts.note: x is the classic algebraic unknown
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A mystery fish whose skeleton might show up in a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: Fish bones make the reader picture a fishbone, but the bones are those of a patient in a hospital image.
explanation.definitionFit: An X-ray photograph shows the skeleton because radiation passes through soft tissue but is blocked by bone.

clue.text: Vocalist, one shouting after swallowing too many drugs

indicators.note: what is swallowed goes inside, so one piece takes another into itself

parts.note: a yeller is one who yells or shouts
OD is short for overdose

explanation.surface: A singer starts shouting after taking an overdose.
explanation.walkthrough: The overdose is not a cause of the shouting but letters swallowed by the shouter.
explanation.definitionFit: A yodeller is a singer who switches rapidly between chest voice and falsetto, as in Alpine folk music.

clue.text: Content to leave Zimbabwe with many a fanatic

indicators.note: when the contents leave, only the outside shell remains, so just the ends are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters
a lot means many

explanation.surface: Happy to leave Zimbabwe along with many a fanatic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' reads as happy, but it is the noun, the insides of a word, which are emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealot is someone with extreme, uncompromising enthusiasm for a cause, just as a fanatic is.
